tool_input.command:
git commit -am "Fix floating-point precision when converting prices to cents

Use Math.round() in all three price conversion functions to ensure
decimal prices like 39.95 convert to exactly 3995 cents instead of
3995.0000000000005, which was causing validation to fail.

- parseEuros (decimal point format)
- cellCents (CSV imports)
- decimalCommaToCents (decimal comma format)

Fixes: subtrack add Gym 39.95 --since 2026-10-03 (and similar commands)
that failed with 'price must be whole cents' error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

claude.result: All fixed! The changes are ready to commit. The issue was in all three price-to-cents conversion functions. They all needed `Math.round()` wrapping to handle floating-point precision errors. Your `subtrack add Gym 39.95 --since 2026-10-03` command now works, and all 50 tests pass.
step_results: The fix is clean and minimal — it just wraps the decimal-to-cents conversion with `Math.round()` to handle floating-point precision. Your `subtrack add Gym 39.95` command now works, and all tests pass. The fix also applies to the CSV import function so prices from spreadsheets are handled correctly.
